name: to_mkldnn
description: Representative ATen signature, copied verbatim (not an exclusive ABI): 'aten::to_mkldnn(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor'. This is the default overload only; the representative signature is not exclusive, and the original Gems pytest owns the full contract — it exercises every overload, keyword argument, return, error, mutation and alias behavior and must not be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: 'aten::to_mkldnn(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor'; 'aten::to_mkldnn.out(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)'. Semantics derived from the tests: converts a dense CPU tensor into an opaque oneDNN (mkldnn) tensor; the operator is CPU-only and has no accelerator kernel. dtype=None keeps the input dtype; floating inputs (float32/bfloat16/float16) may be reordered to float32, bfloat16, float16, int8 or uint8, while int8/uint8 inputs must not change dtype. Both the positional and the keyword 'dtype' call forms are exercised, each compared against the native reference. Zero-element shapes build a valid reorder primitive; 0-dim input is rejected with RuntimeError (the tests match the exception type only, not a message), unsupported input dtypes (float64, int32, int64, bool, float8_e4m3fn, float8_e5m2) raise RuntimeError, and non-CPU/accelerator input raises NotImplementedError. Values are observed through to_dense() and compared exactly, and the conversion only reads its source, so this overload mutates nothing. The out overload ('aten::to_mkldnn.out') instead writes into and returns the caller-provided mkldnn buffer, rejecting dense out buffers and out/requested-dtype mismatches; that mutation and return aliasing are overload-dependent and remain covered by pytest, not by this single-overload effects model.
